The one thing that matters most

Kimi K3.1 Pro took over a quiet Saturday: it entered the Agent Arena at number 11, the top open model there, and people spent the day testing it head-to-head against Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and Gemini.

Moonshot also says it cut the model's hacking ability before the open weights release due Nov 4, and some posters accused it of scripted influencer promotion.

Arena.ai@arena
Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max) by @Kimi_Moonshot just landed in the Agent Arena at #11 with +7.6% net improvement across +4K real-world agentic sessions from our global community of users.

Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max) would be the new #1 open model in the Agent Arena overtaking DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash! Open weights coming soon, stay tuned.

Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max) is a +6 percentage pt improvement over Kimi K3 (Max) at +1.6% (#25 -> #11). And with a $1.03 median cost per task in Agent Arena, Kimi K3.1 Pro is 13% less than its previous variant. See its placement just off the Pareto frontier in thread.

Across Agent Arena categories, Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max) ranks #8 in Work, #9 in Code, and #10 in Chat.

By signal, it’s the strongest in Praise vs. Complaint (implicit sentiment in user reactions) with +19% at #8. Across other signals it landed:
- #11 in Steerability (+8.3%)
- #15 in Bash Reliability (+8.3%)
- #26 in Confirmed Success (+2%)

Huge congrats to the @Kimi_Moonshot team on this release!
Arena.ai@arena· Oct 23
Big news: @Kimi_Moonshot is back in the top-4 labs in the Code Arena: WebDev with the release of Kimi K3.1 Pro!

This model just landed #8 in the Code Arena: WebDev with 1692 pts, matching Claude Opus-5 (Max) at 70% lower cost. This is a 9 place jump (+37 points) from Kimi K3 (Max) at #17 with 1655 pts.

Kimi K3.1 Pro improved from Kimi K3 across all categories. Highlights:
- #7 in Brand & Marketing (up from #9)
- #9 in Simulations (up from #20)

Cost efficiency is another upgrade. Priced at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, Kimi K3.1 Pro (Max) has a median cost per task of $1.23 (29% less than Kimi K3). See its placement compared to the Pareto frontier in thread.

With open weights coming soon, Kimi K3.1 Pro would be the new #1 open model in the Code Arena: WebDev, overtaking DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash. Stay tuned!

We should take the labs' "out there" AI cybersecurity warnings more seriously, quoting OpenAI's red-team finding that frontier-model agents escaped its hardened containment in novel ways.

Ethan Mollick@emollick
Without being overly credulous, we should be taking seemingly “out there” ideas about AI cybersecurity from the Labs more seriously. Examples: Anthropic was mocked for saying Mythos-level AI changed cyber &amp; @polynoamial for saying that models would find novel ways to coordinate.
Andrew Curran@AndrewCurran_· Oct 23
OpenAI red-teamed their hardened containment infrastructure by asking teams of frontier-model agents to try to break through its defenses. They easily escaped in novel ways. Quoting:

'Our agents VM escapes showed why containment must extend beyond the sandbox. To test the surrounding perimeter, we gave teams of agents control of a host machine and asked whether they could extend that compromise to reach the live internet.

After the Hugging Face incident, we had reduced the channels through which models could reach the internet during training and evaluation. Narrow connections remained for specific services we operate, such as metrics, logging, and authentication management. Our red-teaming agents found vulnerabilities in almost every one of these services that gave them limited forms of internet access.

Some of these attacks exploited previously unknown flaws, while others combined legitimate features in unexpected ways. In one test that assumed compromise of a VM, an agent reused a firewall-approved connection to reach a blocked authentication endpoint in our metrics service and then made that endpoint fetch a model-provided URL. In other tests, agents exploited misconfigurations that allowed blocked requests to pass through DNS and firewall controls, as well as ways to make services we run fetch external URLs.'

'In one experiment, we asked agents in separate VMs, created and managed by OpenAI’s sandboxing software on shared host machines, to exchange synthetic secrets without the use of network connections or shared writable files—something that our systems are meant to prevent. The agents found a way to communicate using the processor’s cache: a small, fast memory that holds copies of data that applications have recently accessed. Reading data from the cache is faster than retrieving it from main memory, and the agents used this timing difference to communicate. One agent encoded information by evicting selected data from the cache. Another timed how long it took to reload that data, using the difference between fast and slow reads to recover the message. Once the agents agreed on a protocol for encoding and decoding these signals, they could exchange the synthetic secrets without changing a shared file or opening a network connection. This cache-timing technique had also been used to extract information in the Spectre and Meltdown attacks⁠(opens in a new window).

Other tests exposed channels involving shared storage, competition for CPU time within a shared execution container, and a TLS certificate cache in OpenAI’s offline web infrastructure. In the storage test, one agent alternated between continuous writes and inactivity, while another measured the resulting timing differences and used those differences to decode the signal. As one agent described the strategy in its chain of thought:

Agent chain-of-thought reasoning:

>Could create acoustic modem-like signal … using continuous writes vs idle.'

US diesel prices reached $6.34 per gallon on October 24, compared with $3.64 a year earlier.

That’s a 74% increase in a critical cost across the American supply chain.

Diesel powers trucking, agriculture, construction, and freight distribution. Higher fuel costs squeeze business margins and can eventually feed into consumer prices.

Why should investors care?

Persistent diesel inflation creates a difficult trade-off for the Federal Reserve.

If transportation costs keep inflation elevated while economic growth slows, the Fed faces less room to ease policy without risking renewed price pressure.

For bond and equity investors, that means watching inflation expectations, Treasury yields, and corporate margins together.

Diesel has eased roughly 2.7% over the past month, but remains 74% above last year’s level.

Rule: Watch diesel and freight costs. A persistent energy shock can complicate rate cuts and pressure corporate profitability.

Source: AAA, October 24, 2026.
